scope.reason: The stem asks besides distance; option c repeats distance and adds an unobservable always. It can be rejected by language rather than comparing the illustrated near/far lanes.
Shoot before receiving is impossible with Navy2 still owning the puck; old plan without looking supplies another giveaway. The changed-pressure read is barely tested.
YOU never owned this loose puck, so assume YOU still own it contradicts initial state. Key correctly separates arrival from control but two careless alternatives trivialize that read.

A wide carrier does not necessarily require abandoning an already useful inside recovery line. Stay on your old line may be reasonable if it protects middle and teammate spacing; no new geometry establishes otherwise.
A pass toward the side changes puck read but does not by itself require defender movement toward that puck; middle responsibility and Navy2 spacing may favor another line.
The only sensible choice is a teammate or unspecified clear space; competitor options are unchecked coverage and deliberate pass to an opponent.
New lane and pressure is the sole actual read. Circle name and blind pass are not plausible alternative spatial decisions; no exact changed route is supplied.
Assuming F2 already received before YOU pick up a still-loose puck is impossible in stated sequence; regardless also disqualifies the other distractor.
Both rejected options expressly avoid rechecking. The U11 support comparison can be answered without locating any actor.
Only a is a conditional support call; b promises unchanged openness and c imposes an unrelated never-move instruction on F2.
Notice where D1 follows presupposes a following action not stated in this freeze. Basic support key is otherwise reasonable, but compare position without inventing motion.
F2 lane opens directly announces checking inside pass; other choices invoke always or guarantees rather than actual competing puck decisions.
Reconsider pace, direction or outlet includes nearly every sensible action. Other options demand outdated information or unchecked availability, so no U11 scene-based comparison is needed.
The new clear lane makes shot reconsideration plausible, but c duplicates shooting with without checking and b uses only to exclude alternatives. Answer is supplied by stem plus sensible wording.

Keep the original assignment without looking again.: Ignores newly stated D1 call; keeping assignment can be valid only after reassessing. Automatically skate to the far corner.: Far-corner destination has no cue and is out of category.

Skate to D2’s old location without looking.: D2 old spot is opponent outlet, not YOUR destination; no new cue supports it. Keep charging the exact original line.: Charging exact line advertises reckless rigidity rather than plausible controlled pursuit.
Whether F2 is up ice regardless of the lane: F2 up-ice continuation is legitimately worth scanning; regardless wording artificially disqualifies it.

Follow F2’s route without checking D1’s new lane: Following can remain useful after checking D1, so without checking supplies giveaway. Hold the old return point without checking F2’s route: Old support may remain useful; unchecked wording hides that legitimate alternative.

Bank the puck without looking because D1 moved: Bank the puck assigns action to non-owner YOU unless explicitly advising F1; without looking giveaway too. Pass through D1 to the original spot: Pass through D1 to old spot implies unsupported release by receiver and offers no plausible tradeoff.
Force a shot without checking the goalie or lane: Force and without checking make no credible rival choice. Ignore F2 because D1 moved: Ignoring genuine F2 outlet after defender moves is arbitrary.

Leave both attackers to chase the puck: Leave both attackers to chase puck is internally odd: F1 owns that puck. Stay on F2 without checking F1: Staying F2 may remain appropriate after reassessment; without checking removes plausible alternative.

Continue backchecking F2 without looking: Backchecking may become protective support, but without looking makes stale behavior wrong by wording. Assume F2 still controls the puck: F2 never controls in setup or hypothetical; still controls invents prior possession.

A pass to F2 deserves consideration, but the changed shooting line does not rule out a controlled carry that changes the angle. The unchecked shot is a giveaway alternative. Root accepts the independent revision finding over the primary retention.
The assumption that maximum speed always helps: Maximum speed always helps is unobservable universal, not a cue.
Shoot without checking the blocker: Unobserved shooting is behavior, not same-category scene change; shot itself changes puck position too, so wording logically muddled.
A promise that a turn always beats the defender: Promise always beats is not observable check; answerable on wording.
Turn again without checking F2: Turn without checking teammate is artificial bad behavior. Carry into Gold 1’s approach by default: Carry into pressure by default is artificial bad behavior.
A fixed distance rule regardless of the play: Fixed-distance rule regardless ignores context; not a competing observed cue.
Remain beside the wall and ignore the pass: Ignoring new pass is obvious refusal to update. Complete the old approach regardless: Complete regardless is another giveaway.
Keep marking the empty spot Gold 2 left: Marking empty old spot is caricature of spatial coverage. Chase the half-wall puck without checking: Unchecked chase discards named Gold2 responsibility.
How to chase exactly behind Gold 1 regardless of support: Exact trailing chase regardless removes teammate coordination by wording.
Whether two defenders near every puck is always better: Two defenders near every puck always better is absurd general rule, not observation.
You must always take several extra touches: Always extra touches is universal unrelated to actual reception. Gold 1 no longer needs to be checked: Gold1 remains relevant despite flat arrival.
Shoot through Gold 1 without checking: Shoot-through without checking is poor behavior, also not YOUR current action.
Skating wide without looking: Wide skating without looking is not a cue; automatic elimination.
The original shooting lane, without checking Gold 2 or D1: Old shot without checking both actors deliberately nonsensical.
Stay opposite regardless of puck: Stay regardless is bad by qualifier, though maintaining opposite outlet can help.

Continue deep into the offensive zone: Continuing forward can remain useful if puck still available; no new possession evidence. Skate beside W without checking Gold 2: W unchecked approach lacks Gold2 scan and advertises mistake.
Whether a rim always requires a pinch: Every rim requires pinch is universal, not visible cue; too obvious for U15.
The same low pass without checking Gold 1: Low pass without checking removes plausible F2 option by wording. An automatic shot through Gold 2: Automatic shot through Gold2 is giveaway.
The power play removes all pressure: Powerplay removes all pressure plainly false. F2 is the next receiver regardless of Gold 1’s position: F2 regardless prevents conditional comparison.
Completing the offensive rotation without looking: Unchecked rotation plainly stale. Treating F2 as the carrier anyway: F2-as-carrier contradicts explicitly stated Gold2 gain.
The reset regardless of Gold 2’s movement: Reset regardless excludes observation. An assumption that both routes are still equally covered: Equal coverage assumption unsupported even before move.
Return the puck low without looking: Blind low return automatically wrong by wording. Shoot automatically because YOU are high: Automatic shot from high position no guarantee.

The slot is always covered: Slot always covered false certainty. F1 stays the low outlet even when the carrier angle changes: F1 can remain low when carrier angle changes; being outlet location does not guarantee reachability, so c ambiguous.
Assuming the same receiver is always open: Always-open assumption not cue.
The puck side never changes: Never changes contradicts prompt, not plausible cue.
A high support spot chosen without checking F2’s lane: Unchecked spot choice is not a detail; obvious out-of-category distractor.
Force F1 because Gold 2 moved: Force F1 because marker moved towards F1 is implausible. Use D2 without checking the carrier angle: D2 may be valid reset; without checking disqualifies by wording.
Drop beside F2 without checking the slot: Unchecked drop beside teammate giveaway. Shoot because the slot defender moved: YOU have no puck; shoot because marker moves impossible before receipt.
The change requires a dump regardless of pressure: Mandatory dump from line change is artificial universal, not cue.
Leave the puck without checking the new lane: Leaving puck without checking is irrelevant action. Assume the change makes every route safe: Every route safe from one new teammate clearly false.
Force F2 because the defender moved: Force from movement alone misreads availability. Send the puck low without checking F1: Unobserved low send obvious; F1 lane must account net/defenders.

The clock makes every forward pass automatically wrong: Clock forbids every forward pass contradicted directly in briefing. D2 must receive regardless of the open route: D2 mandatory regardless no tactical alternative.

The lead removes every forward option: Lead forbids forward directly contradicted by briefing. F1 is the first outlet regardless of the pressure route: F1 predetermined regardless pressure not realistic rival call.
A certainty that shooting from the point always scores: Point shot always scores cartoon certainty, not U18 assessment.

The old activation regardless of possession: Possession-ignoring activation breaches drill condition. A belief that D2 can cover every possible turnover alone: D2 covers every turnover alone impossible assurance.
A requirement to pass first-time regardless: First-time regardless contradicts explicit permitted-not-required premise.
Force a shot because the lead is close: Force shot because close lead is arbitrary. Dump without checking support: Unchecked dump giveaway, though controlled placement could sometimes be sensible.

Stay on the original Gold 2 spot: Mark empty original position not a real competing assignment. Follow the puck without checking the slot: Unchecked puck follow discards explicit confirmed-cover rule.
